About Us
Learning and Achieving Together
Hillingdon Primary School is an academy school situated on the Uxbridge Road in the area known as Hillingdon Heath. There has been a school on the site for over 100 years. It is a warm, welcoming and inclusive school that values the diverse community that it serves.
Learning and achievement drives everything that we do at Hillingdon Primary School. Our job, in partnership with parents and carers, is to build the foundations for a successful education, readying children for each stage. We also enable each child to discover the joy of learning, to help them to fulfil every aspect of their potential and to encourage their growth into effective citizens, ready to play their part positively in their community and modern Britain.
We believe that every child is able to be successful in the key areas of English and Maths, and we are keen to see this recognised in the results they secure. However, we also want them to learn and experience more than this through an ambitious and varied curriculum, and a range of extracurricular opportunities and school clubs that complement our work in the classroom.
We value each child as an individual and aim to provide the opportunities for pupils to excel in areas where they have a special talent, whether this is in science, in sport, in drama, in art, in music or through involvement in our school community council.
This website offers an insight into our school – a glimpse of our values, curriculum, events and community. If you would like to know more then you are encouraged to contact the school office and arrange a visit to see us at work.
Sabrina Kelly and Samina Saidiya Co-Principals
Our school's aims
At Hillingdon Primary School our mission is to ensure that everyone is happy, caring and independent, and that our school is a place where we can learn together and do our best.
Our aims are for every child to...
Be happy, safe, confident, responsible and independent in a secure, stimulating environment which provides positive opportunities for success for all, with everyone feeling they belong;
Enjoy acquiring knowledge, skills and abilities in all areas of the curriculum;
Take increasing responsibility for their learning within a stimulating, structured environment where expectations are high;
Develop, through a variety of learning experiences, creativity, problem-solving skills, the ability to make informed choices and the enthusiasm for discovery that will remain the basis for future learning;
Show respect, kindness and care for everyone in the school community, and to recognise and value their own contribution and that made by others to its general well-being; and
Develop further understanding and respect for our diverse community, both locally and in the wider world, and for our environment.

Reception 2027 Admission - Information for Prospective Parents and Carers
We understand that choosing the right primary school for your child is a huge decision that takes time and careful consideration. We are thrilled that you are considering Hillingdon Primary School for your child and that you are visiting our website to learn more about our school.
This page has been designed to provide parents and carers with quick links to more detailed information about key areas of school life: these are areas that prospective parents and carers frequently ask about when contacting the school.
If you do not find the information you are looking for here, please feel free to use the search function at the top right-hand side of the home page, or alternatively email our school office at hillprimary@hillingdonprimaryschool.org.uk and one of our office team will be happy to help you.
We are thrilled that you are considering Hillingdon Primary School as the school of choice for your child's education and that you would like to attend one of our Open Days to learn more about our school, meet our senior leadership team and have a tour of our premises.
Our Open Days for admission in September 2027 will be held on:
Places must be pre-booked to ensure we can accommodate everyone and maintain a safe environment for our school community and visitors. As our Open Days are usually very popular, we request that you do not bring your children to the Open Day: this will ensure that as many parents as possible are able to attend on their chosen day.
Please complete the following form to register your attendance at one of our Open Days. We will be allocating places on a first come, first served basis.
https://forms.gle/cGLLWRofd96nfPXg8
We are proud to be part of the Elliot Foundation Academies Trust (TEFAT): a successful mulit-academy trust specialising in the Primary sector. Please click here to learn more about TEFAT and its vision and values.
All applications must be made via the London Borough of Hillingdon: please visit their website at: https://www.hillingdon.gov.uk/primary for further details, including important deadlines for submitting your application.
To learn more about how we allocate places at Hillingdon Primary School, please visit our Admissions page to view our School Admission Policy and associated information.

Safeguarding Out of Hours Contact Information
Guidance on Reporting a Safeguarding Concern Out of School Hours
Worried about a child out of school hours?
If a child is in immediate danger or at risk of immediate harm, you should contact the Police on 999
If you are concerned about a child you should share your concern with our local Children’s Social Care Service by calling Hillingdon Children's Services/Stronger Families Hub on 01895 556006 or email StrongerFamiliesHub@hillingdon.gov.uk
You can also contact the NSPCC for advice on 0808 800 5000 or email help@NSPCC.org.uk
If you have non-urgent information about the safety or welfare of a child to share with the safeguarding team at Hillingdon Primary School then please email safeguarding@hillingdonprimaryschool.org.uk.
Please note, this email is only monitored once daily during school holidays, it is not monitored during weekends.
Please see our School Hours Safeguarding Contact Information page for guidance on who to contact to raise a concern during school hours, including the names of our Designated Safeguarding Leads.
If you need an immediate response or if you are concerned for a child’s immediate safety or welfare please contact the Police.
Cookie Policy
Safeguarding Contact Information

Breakfast Club
The school offers a Breakfast Club for students from Reception to Year 6.
The Breakfast Club opens at 7:30am, providing care and supervision for our students until the school day begins.
The Breakfast Club costs £5 per day and places must be pre-booked and paid for in advance. If your child's place is not pre-booked, the charge increases to £6 a session. Payment is made online via ParentPay. The school is also signed up to the Government's Tax Free Childcare scheme and Childcare Grant Payment Service for parents and carers who are eligible for support with their childcare costs.
Pupils must arrive by 8:15am. They will receive a snack, however they should also have eaten breakfast at home.
Please email wraparoundcare@hillingdonprimaryschool.org.uk for further information, including terms and conditions and details of how to book.

Early Years and Foundation Stage Curriculum
At Hillingdon Primary School, we fully embrace the four guiding principles which shape the EYFS curriculum:
There are seven areas of learning and development
These 7 areas are used to plan your child’s learning and activities. The professionals teaching and supporting your child will make sure that activities are suited to your child’s unique needs. They are designed to be really flexible so that staff can follow your child's needs and interests.
Children in the EYFS learn by playing and exploring, being active, and through creative and critical thinking, which takes place both indoors and outside.
At the end of Reception our children will be assessed against the Early Learning Goals, and their progress shared with parents.

pageCache.pageTitle: Hillingdon Primary School - Nursery and Reception Transition
pageCache.text:
Nursery and Reception Transition
Hillingdon Primary School Nursery Transition
Beginning of July: Nursery open day – an opportunity for all parents and pupils starting in the nursery in September, to visit the nursery and meet the nursery staff.
September: Hillingdon Primary School staff visit children’s homes to meet children and parents prior to starting: We try to visit all new children and parents in their homes, so that we can get to know them better and find out information about their learning and development.
September: We operate a staggered start for Nursery Children, so that children have the chance to start in small groups. Further details about your child’s start date will be given to you at the home visits. All parents will be able to come into the nursery to ensure their child is settled in and also ask staff any questions.
Part-time pupils will attend the nursery for morning sessions (8:45am – 11:45am) or afternoon sessions (12:15pm – 3:15pm).
Full-time pupils will attend the nursery from 9am – 3pm. A half an hour lunchtime is included in this session.
October: Nursery Parents’ Curriculum Evening: An opportunity to find out how your child will be learning in Nursery at Hillingdon Primary School.
Further details will be sent out prior to each event.
Hillingdon Primary School Reception Transition
Beginning of June: Hillingdon Primary School staff visit children’s nurseries to meet children prior to starting: We try to visit all new children in their nurseries so that we can get to know them better and find out information about their learning from their current teachers.
Beginning of July: Information sessions for all parents of Reception. An opportunity to meet the team at Hillingdon Primary School and find out information about starting school. During these sessions, you will have a chance to meet your child’s class teacher and gather information including details of the school day and uniform requirements.
Unfortunately we are unable to provide crèche facilities, so parents are asked not to bring children to these sessions.
September: We operate a staggered start for Reception Children, so that children have the chance to start school in small groups. Further details about your child’s start date will be given to you at the information sessions.
We look forward to working with you and your child. If you have any further queries, please contact the Admissions Officer at admissions@hillingdonprimaryschool.org.uk or phone 01895 590087.
Cookie Policy

pageCache.pageTitle: Hillingdon Primary School - Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE) Policy Consultation
pageCache.text:
Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE) Policy Consultation
Update: This consultation is now complete
Thank you to everyone who responded to our Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE) consultation. A link to the final RSHE Policy can be found below.
In response to feedback from parents, we have provided more detailed information on the content of the 'Relationships' and 'Changing Me' elements of our Curriculum, including a list of vocabulary used. This information can be found on the Personal Development page of our website.
We will be addressing the common themes, questions and concerns raised during the consultation at our parent workshop on Friday 3rd July at 14:30.
Consultation Information
The Department for Education have issued new statutory guidance for Relationships, Sex, and Health Education (RSHE) introducing updated, age-appropriate content across all schools. Key changes feature a greater focus on digital safety, AI awareness, misogyny, personal safety, and mental health. At Hillingdon Primary School, these changes will come into effect from the Autumn term of 2026.
In preparation for implementing the new requirements, we have reviewed our curriculum and made changes to our Relationships, Sex and Health Education Policy so we can be sure our provision meets all legal requirements and is appropriate for our pupils based on their age; physical and emotional maturity; religious and cultural backgrounds; and special educational needs and/or disabilities.
We know that both parents, carers and schools play a key role in the education of children and we are keen to receive parents' and carers' feedback on the revised policy. We wrote to all parents and carers on Tuesday 2nd June to provide details of the consultation and copies of all relevant documentation. The consultation will run for two weeks, closing at 3:30pm on Tuesday 16th June 2026.
Please see below for copies of the following consultation documents:
Please click here to submit your feedback via our online Google form before 3:30pm on Tuesday 16th June 2026.
Please take the time to read the policy and DfE guide prior to submitting your feedback as both provide key information about the school’s legal obligations, the content of the curriculum, why we are being asked to teach it and our delivery of the curriculum. Please be aware that while your views are welcome and will be genuinely reflected upon to reach our final outcome, they cannot amount to a veto over curriculum content. The law requires the school to teach Relationships and Health Education to all primary school children.
If for any reason you can’t complete the Google Form, please speak to the school office and we will make alternative arrangements for you to participate in the consultation.
Workshop: We will be holding a parent workshop on Friday 3rd July at 2:30pm, during which we will aim to address any themes, questions or concerns raised through the parent feedback form.
